title: The Region 6 Wrap: Brazil's Real Jumps 7%, a Wider Dominican Deficit | Across the Water, Ep. 26
lede: The week of Nov 23 in the business of the African diaspora: the US dollar falls 7.03% against Brazil's real after Bradesco chair Luiz Carlos Trabuco is confirmed as finance minister from 2027, Brazil's fiscal adjustment becomes law, Sebrae finds Black business owners earn 56% of what white owners do, the Dominican Senate widens the 2026 deficit to 4.2% of GDP, and a CARICOM study puts the cost of cleaner shipping at US$3.6 billion. Plus Caribbean currencies and Small Business Saturday.
keyPoints: The dollar closed at R$5.514 on Nov 27, down 7.03% on the week, as Luiz Carlos Trabuco was confirmed to run Brazil's Finance Ministry from 2027 (A Rede, Metrópoles).

Brazil's fiscal adjustment passed the lower house unchanged and was signed without vetoes as Complementary Law 239; the government estimates a R$45.1–56.1 billion gain to the 2027 primary result (Agência Câmara, NTVB).
Black business owners in Brazil earned R$2,832 a month on average in Q2 2026, 56% of white owners' R$5,038 (Sebrae, Nov 20).

The Dominican Senate voted 23–1 on Nov 24 to raise the 2026 deficit from 3.24% to 4.2% of GDP, with RD$54.1 billion of extra spending, while October activity grew 5.4% (Diario Libre, Banco Central via Infobae).
A CARICOM Private Sector Organisation study estimates the IMO net-zero framework could add US$3.6 billion to the region's shipping costs over 2028–2035 (Jamaica Observer, Nov 27).
